### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/operation-private-keys.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/operation-private-keys.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **47** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `90aac88085c87d1712e50f76e3cdd5ed7bf9c378` — the merge of head `dc070731cbfedabd32e6dab710aa82686491b2c5` into base `24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 90aac88085c87d1712e50f76e3cdd5ed7bf9c378 && git checkout 90aac88085c87d1712e50f76e3cdd5ed7bf9c378
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6 dc070731cbfedabd32e6dab710aa82686491b2c5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6 && git merge --no-ff dc070731cbfedabd32e6dab710aa82686491b2c5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review: PASS

Head: `dc070731cbfedabd32e6dab710aa82686491b2c5` · reviewer review#2 (`session_016WV4czuuneAppDnJbrNejw`) · area A3 · Fixes #33051

`Clause-②: no` is right: no authorable key, value or type moves. Each operation now reads at the depth resolved for its own object.

Checked:
- Step 2.6 now collects `__readScope` / `__writeScope`, the delegator halves and the external grant stamp (`externalGrantPatch`, the existing pure twin of `stampExternalGrant`: same key, same `object`-or-`undefined` value) into `operationStamps` instead of assigning them onto `opCtx.context`. The read/write verb lists and the values are unchanged.
- The copy `{ ...opCtx.context, ...operationStamps }` is made right before `next()`, after step 3, so request-wide memos staged on the caller's envelope above (`__rlsMembershipStaged`, membership keys, queues) are carried into it. The caller's envelope is never written.
- Readers: every consumer of these keys reads the envelope it is handed. `buildSharingMiddleware` reads `ctx.context` at entry and passes it to `buildReadFilter` / `buildWriteFilter` (incl. the delegator re-runs built from `exec.__delegator*Scope`); `sharing-service.ts` reads `__readScope` / `__writeScope` from the context argument; `externalGrantSpeaks` reads the context argument. `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts` and `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` build their own envelopes with explicit scopes. Nothing in the authz middleware between step 2.6 and `next()`, or after it, reads a stamp back from the caller's envelope; the post-`next()` seam check reads `writeImageCheckSeam`, not the context.
- Writes: `update` / `delete` / `transfer` / `restore` / `purge` take the write depth on the same copy, so `buildWriteFilter` and `canEdit` downstream read it (the `authz-matrix-gate` and D10 write-leg tests read it from `opCtx.context`).
- Nested operations: a nested operation started downstream with the copy goes through the middleware again and gets its own copy, so the parent's depth is not overwritten under it either. An operation with no permission sets gets no copy and no stamp; `buildReadFilter` then resolves the owner set with no depth, which is the narrowest reading.
- Tests: the unit tests read the stamps from `opCtx.context` and assert the caller's envelope has none (`not.toHaveProperty('__readScope')`, external grant unchanged on the caller). The dogfood pin drives the record page with two related slices in both orders and asserts each slice equals the same slice read alone, for an org-depth object and for a private object beside it.
- The `operation-private-keys.ts` change is comment-only.

Before landing: checks on this head were still running when I read it (11 success, 10 skipped, 15 in progress, none failed). This PASS holds for this head once they are all green. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` is also touched by #33290 (different hunks): whichever lands second needs a clean merge of main; a conflict-free merge keeps this PASS.

No findings.
